definitions.explanation: The outermost or topmost layer of something physical, such as the earth's surface, skin, or a body of water.
The outward or shallow aspect of something, as opposed to its deeper, underlying reality. Used figuratively.

examples.japanese: {海|うみ}の{表層|ひょうそう}は{暖|あたた}かい。
examples.english: The surface layer of the ocean is warm.

examples.japanese: {地盤|じばん}の{表層|ひょうそう}を{調査|ちょうさ}する。
examples.english: To survey the surface layer of the ground.

examples.japanese: {表層|ひょうそう}の{土|つち}を{取|と}り{除|のぞ}くと、{岩盤|がんばん}が{現|あらわ}れた。
examples.english: When the surface layer of soil was removed, bedrock appeared.

examples.japanese: {表層|ひょうそう}だけを{見|み}ていてはだめだ。
examples.english: You can't just look at the surface.

examples.japanese: {表層的|ひょうそうてき}な{理解|りかい}にとどまっている。
examples.english: The understanding remains only at a superficial level.

examples.japanese: {問題|もんだい}の{表層|ひょうそう}だけでなく、{根本|こんぽん}{原因|げんいん}を{探|さぐ}る{必要|ひつよう}がある。
examples.english: We need to look beyond the surface of the problem and investigate the root cause.

notes:
Describes the outermost layer of something, used both literally (geology, oceanography, skin) and figuratively (shallow understanding, surface-level analysis). Contrasts with {深層|しんそう} (deep layer).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {表層|ひょうそう}{水|すい}: surface water
- {表層|ひょうそう}{地盤|じばん}: surface ground
- {表層的|ひょうそうてき}: superficial
- {表層|ひょうそう}を{掘|ほ}る: to dig the surface layer

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {表層|ひょうそう} (surface) ↔ {深層|しんそう} (deep layer) — this pair is used extensively in both literal (geology, oceanography) and figurative (psychology, analysis) contexts

ETYMOLOGY:
{表|ひょう} (surface, outside) + {層|そう} (layer, stratum).
